original_test_intent: Demonstrate on the intended Intel GNR DIMM that an injected correctable memory error is consumed by Patrol Scrub and produces the expected firmware-first machine-check, retry-read and ELog `extlog_mem_event` evidence without escalating unexpectedly.
original_method: Record platform/CPU/BIOS/BMC/OS/DIMM topology and approved Intel harness; preserve baseline logs and BIOS/GRUB settings; apply and verify the exact source BIOS matrix with reboot as required; map the harness address and selected mc2/ch0/DIMM to the intended target; verify patrol scrub, interval, ECS, PTRR and en_patspr; preserve then clear only the approved MC/retry test registers; halt through CScripts, reset the injector lock, issue the literal CE PatrolConsume injection once, inspect the named shadow/MSCOD and retry logs, resume, collect serial/FTrace/ELog/extlog_mem_event/OS/BMC evidence, verify health, and restore all settings through an approved recovery plan.
manual_activity: An Intel-qualified owner/FAE applies BIOS/DFX settings, validates the address-to-DIMM mapping and drives halt/injection/go/recovery; the agent may capture and correlate approved register, serial, ELog, OS and BMC evidence.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute one topology-bound patrol-consumed CE under qualified CScripts control and correlate the exact scrub, MCA/retry, firmware ELog and platform logs before restoring security settings.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds immutable target mapping, preexisting-log preservation, explicit result decoders, severity stops and audited restoration while retaining the source sequence.

modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Low-level debug unlock and memory injection can hang/crash the system or affect the wrong DIMM when address/topology mapping is wrong.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row157 Wistron-System RAS-00114-V008: approve GNR CPU stepping/BIOS/BMC/OS, CScripts harness version/hash/license, project mapping and restoration for every listed BIOS/GRUB knob, socket/IMC/channel/DIMM plus address0x8000/mc2.ch0/en_patspr mapping, safe MC/retry baseline-clear semantics, expected scrubctl, correctable MSCOD/retry/extlog_mem_event fields and timestamp correlation, and halt/go/crash/OOB recovery with no automatic reinjection.

review_improvement: Preserves the exact patrol-consumed injector and source register paths, rejects generic truncated logs as acceptance, protects historical evidence and requires topology, decoder, recovery and security-setting restoration.
independent_technical_reasoning: Patrol Scrub is a background consumer; the essential distinction from Demand Scrub is that the harness injects a latent CE with PatrolConsume and the scrub engine later detects it. A corrected OS log alone does not identify that consumer. The selected mc2/ch0 paths and address 0x8000 are platform/harness coordinates that must map to the intended DIMM. Firmware-first handling also means the decisive evidence spans MCA shadow, retry log, serial firmware response and extlog_mem_event. Unlocking DFX and disabling locks changes platform security and must be reversed even if the injection succeeds.
